verdict.why: The right build has a hipped-and-gabled dark tile roof with upturned eave tips, timber-framed walls with white panels, stone footings, a stone lantern, and a stone path set in a garden, so it reads as a tea house, while the left is a stepped, pagoda-like dark block on a stone plinth with no visible engawa, lantern, or garden setting; the right also has the more varied finish and palette, though its roof is somewhat blocky and it shows no clear maple.

Left shows the brief's defining features: a dark tiled hipped-and-gabled roof with upturned eave corners, a raised timber floor on stone footings, lanterns, and a garden setting with stepping stones and greenery. Right is a monolithic stepped pyramid in one dark timber tone with no curved eaves, no visible paper screens, and no garden context, so it reads more like a pagoda or ziggurat than a tea house.

The Right build reads as a desert market hall, with a shaded arcade under striped orange-and-white awnings, crates, barrels, clay pots, a wind-tower or dome top, and wooden beam ends on the front band, while the Left build reads as a walled fortress with crenellations and a central keep and has almost none of the brief's market features.

The Left build has the brief's market features (striped cloth awnings over a shaded street-level arcade, protruding wooden beam ends under a parapet roof, a small domed tower, and sandstone-and-terracotta walls with storefront crates and baskets), while the Right reads as a crenellated castle or fort with grey merlons and no awnings, vigas, or market dressing, even though its walls are cleaner.

The Right build shows the stave-church cues the brief names (carved dragon-head projections at the eaves and gables, stone base with a stone-faced gallery, stacked tiers with a stone-capped roof), so it reads more clearly as a Norwegian stave church, while the Left build reads as a generic stacked pagoda with a plain spire and no dragon heads; but the Right build's craft is messier, with scattered, disordered roof pieces and gaps in its tiers, whereas the Left build's massing and roof stepping are cleaner and more coherent.

Left carries more of the brief's defining features (curled dragon-like eave and gable ornaments, tiered shingled roofs, a stone base, and a spire), while Right is cleaner and more coherent in massing but reads as a generic flat-stepped pagoda with few stave-church cues; Left's roof close-up is messy with stray spikes and chaotic stepping, so the overall lean is only slight.

The left build reads more like a lighthouse, with a tall slender tower, a clear glass lantern room and a railed gallery, while the right looks squatter and more like a turret, but the right has the better finish: a rocky mossy stone base, windowed facades, and a pitched red-tile cottage roof with a stone chimney, whereas the left has jagged stripe artifacts and a grass-island base with little rock.

Left attaches the keeper's cottage to the tower with a clear terracotta pitched roof, chimney, and rocky mossy base, matching the brief's defining features, while Right's lighthouse is taller and more slender but its cottage is detached, open-sided, and reads more like a barn, and its tower shows jagged stepped-edge artifacts.

The Right build has a mossy stone base with lanterns, dark timber-framed upper storeys with white infill, a glowing orange window, and a teal conical roof, so it reads as the brief's wizard tower, while the Left build is a plain purple-trimmed stone shaft with a pointed cap and none of the timber, lanterns, glow, or jetties; the Right roof is lumpy in places, which keeps the craft win from being decisive.

The left build has a stone base, timber-framed jettied floors, lanterns, and a glowing window, so it reads as the brief's building, but its roof is a jumbled teal voxel cone and the massing is stubby and boxy; the right build is a clean, tall, well-proportioned stone tower with a tiered conical roof and a crisp finish, but it lacks timber jetties, a balcony, lanterns, and a glowing window, so it reads less as a wizard tower and more as a generic purple-trimmed spire.

Right has the brief's stone base, jettied timber-framed upper floors, a lantern, a glowing window, a balcony and a leaning conical roof. Left is a plain tall stone shaft with a symmetric purple-and-black cone and little else, so it reads as a generic tower, not a crooked wizard tower.

Left has the brief's defining features: a stone base, timber-framed upper floors that jetty outward, a glowing window, a balcony with a telescope, lanterns and a tall conical roof. Right is a clean, well-finished tower, but it is a straight gray shaft with a neat roof and no jetty, timber framing, crookedness or visible balcony, so it reads as a generic tower rather than a crooked wizard tower.

Right carries more of the brief's defining features (cantilevered roof over a timber soffit, a stone plinth, the tiled terrace with tables, planters and lanterns), while Left is mostly a glass-fronted box with no terrace, planters or soffit; Left is the cleaner build, with a more consistent glazing rhythm and fewer blank walls, but its missing features outweigh that.

The right build reads as a modern glass café: floor-to-ceiling glass bays on the sides and front, a slim dark frame, a cantilevered flat roof with a light stone edge, and a clean plinth, while the left is a dark solid box with a timber-band soffit that reads more like a closed pavilion and shows little glass.

Right has the brief's cantilevered roof with a timber soffit, a concrete plinth, a terrace with tables, planters, lanterns and a sign, even though its roof is a heavy black slab and the back wall is blank; Left is a glazed box with a flat roof, no overhang, no terrace and no sign, so it reads more like an office or a shop than a café.

Right shows the floor-to-ceiling glass, slim dark frame, flat roof and interior furnishing that define a modern café, though it lacks a terrace and sign. Left has a huge black slab roof that hides the building, with a mostly blank black body and a back wall with no detail, even though it has a terrace, planters and an orange sign.

The right build shows the brief's defining features (a cupola with a weather vane, a hoist beam over the loft door, hay bales, a fence, a stone foundation, and white-trimmed doors), while the left has only the red walls, stone band, and doors, with no visible cupola or hay bales; the right's crenellated trim and checkered doors look more castle-like than barn-like, but its detail and finish still beat the left's plain red gable.

The left build carries more of the brief's named features (a visible cupola with weather vane, hay bales, a fence, a stone base, and big white-trimmed doors), but its crenellated roof edges and checkerboard facade make it read partly as a fortress. The right build is cleaner and more coherent in massing and palette, with a stone plinth, timber framing, and a well-resolved gable, yet it has no cupola or vane and its hay bales are barely visible, so it reads more as a red timber house than a farm barn.

The Right build has the brief's defining parts (multiple tall capped chimney stacks, a skylit roof, and a stone-and-brick frame with an open loading bay), while the Left reads as a plain brick house with a striped roof and one chimney; but the Right is ragged, with floating and missing blocks and gaps in its walls, whereas the Left's massing and facades are cleaner and more coherent.

The right build has a legible sawtooth roof, a tall brick chimney, and a ground-floor loading door on a clean brick-and-stone massing, while the left build's flat green roof, scattered protruding copper pipes, and cluttered facades read as a muddled block with no clear sawtooth profile or gear window, though neither shows the round gear window or a crane.

Left is a coherent brick workshop with a sawtooth-like ribbed roof, a tall chimney, a door and a gable window, though its roof is gappy and it has no crane or gear. Right is a messy, chaotic jumble of copper and stone fragments with a flat roof and no clear workshop identity, even though it has skylights and several chimney stacks.

Right is a coherent brick workshop with a sawtooth-style ridged copper roof, a tall chimney, doors and a clean palette, even though its roof is open and slatted. Left is a chaotic box with random copper and stone patches, a flat oxidized lid, stubby chimneys and a ragged, holey facade, and it shows no gear window or crane.
